newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka ruling coalition members in war of words.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka ruling coalition members in war of words.

text.p: Cracks appeared in Sri Lanka's 13-party ruling People's Alliance on Friday after a government minister accused one of his cabinet colleagues of declining to support the coalition in last week's local polls.

Industrial Development Minister C.V. Gonneratne was quoted as saying by newspapers that he had asked President Chandrika Kumaratunga to take action against Transport Minister Srimani Athulathmudali after her group refused to support PA candidates in the polls which were swept by the coalition.
He accused Athulathmudali of declining to join PA's campaign and instead sponsoring an independent group while being in the government.

"If she does not approve of the government's programme of work or if she wished to break away from the government, she should say so in public and get out of the government," Gonneratne was quoted as saying by the independent Island newspaper on Friday.
Gooneratne belongs to the Sri Lanka Freedom Party, the main constituent in PA, and Athulathmudali heads the Democratic United National Lalith Front (DUNLF), which has five seats in parliament.
Kumaratunga's government, which has a one-vote majority in Sri Lanka's 225-seat parliament, relies on the support of coalition members such as the DUNLF and other smaller groups to stay in power.
"Her (Athulathmudali) anti-PA activities were helping the UNP (main opposition United National Party)," the state-owned Daily News quoted Gonneratne as saying.
The PA won 194 of the 238 councils at stake in the elections against UNP's 43.

Athulathmudali herself was not available for comment but her deputy denied the charges and instead said that the DUNLF had stayed away from the polls as it was unhappy over PA's delay in implementing the promises made in its 1994 election manifesto.
"We gave the election a miss, but we did not support any other party or candidate," Ravi Karunanayake, member of parliament and deputy leader of the DUNLF, told Reuters.
"We think it is very unprofessional on the part of a senior government member to utter such things. These allegations are totally unwarranted," he said reacting to Gonneratne's comments.

Karunanayke said his party was committed to the abolition of executive presidency and implementation of devolution proposals, which featured prominently in PA's election manifesto and accused the government of dragging its feet over the issues.
"We are not asking for personal favours here. We are only asking the government to implement its election pledges to the people," Karunanayake said.

Sri Lanka is in the midst of introducing constitutional reforms that would abolish executive presidency and devolve more power to minorities aimed at ending a 13-year-old ethnic war in the island's north and east.
